ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Successively use different AC power supplies to supply power to the same light bulb. The first time, the voltage across the two ends of the light bulb changes with time according to a sinusoidal law (as shown in Figure A); the second time, the law of change of the voltage across the two ends of the light bulb is as shown in Figure B. If the voltage and period values represented by U_0 and T in Figures A and B are the same, then which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: For the first and second times, the ratio of the electric power of the light bulb is 1∶5

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the images: In Figure A of the problem, the vertical axis is voltage u, the horizontal axis is time t, the voltage changes sinusoidally with time, the peak value is marked as U0, the valley value is marked as −U0, and it repeats with period T. In Figure B of the problem, the voltage is a square wave: within each period T, from 0 to T/2 it takes 2U0, from T/2 to T it takes −U0, and afterward it periodically repeats according to the same law. Then reason: the light bulb is the same, so the resistance R may be considered the same, and the average electric power P is proportional to the square of the effective value of the voltage, namely P=U有效^2/R. The first time is sinusoidal alternating current, with maximum value U0, so U1有效^2=U0^2/2. The second time, within one period, the voltage is 2U0 for half a period and −U0 for half a period, therefore U2有效^2=[(2U0)^2·(T/2)+(−U0)^2·(T/2)]/T=(4U0^2/2+U0^2/2)=5U0^2/2. Thus P1:P2=U1有效^2:U2有效^2=(U0^2/2):(5U0^2/2)=1:5.
